review.notes: 'Most of the work it does is digestion' is not just unearned, it is backwards. Saliva's functions are conventionally grouped as lubrication and protection, buffering and clearance, tooth integrity, antimicrobial activity, and taste/digestion - and salivary amylase contributes only a limited share of starch breakdown because most of it is done by pancreatic amylase. The volume figure (two pints, ~1.1 L) is fine, but the ranking is the item's entire point and it is wrong. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

text: Your body makes about two pints of saliva a day, and most of the work it does is digestion that starts before you've swallowed.

text: Cold hands are usually your body being efficient rather than unwell — it narrows the vessels near the skin to keep your core warm, and fingers are the first thing it gives up.

review.notes: 'Almost entirely operated from the forearm' is an unearned proportion, and it is contradicted by this packet's own SF-TRV-000301 explanation, which correctly says the hand's small intrinsic muscles do the fine control. A fast piano passage is precisely fine control - lumbricals and interossei are central to it, not an afterthought. The true core (fingers contain no muscle bellies; the long flexors and extensors are in the forearm) survives without the proportion. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

text: A piano player's hands are almost entirely operated from the forearm. Watch a fast passage and the fingers are the end of the machine, not the machine.

review.notes: Both halves are well established - uphill walking has the higher metabolic cost, downhill is eccentric work and is what produces delayed soreness - so the comparative is earned rather than invented. 'Two different systems, two different bills' is a genuine explanation, not a restatement. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

text: Walking uphill uses more energy than walking downhill, but walking downhill leaves you sorer. Two different systems, two different bills.

There is no comparative fatigue-resistance measurement that puts the tongue ahead of other muscles, and the obvious counter-examples are the heart and the diaphragm, which are more tireless than the tongue by any measure. Drop or hedge the clause and the item is fine. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

review.notes: 'On us it achieves nothing at all' is an absolute that current evidence does not support. The thermoregulatory payoff is indeed lost in humans, but the arrector pili muscle is not functionless: 2020 work in Cell showed it forms part of a dual-component niche with sympathetic nerves that regulates hair follicle stem cells, and cold-driven contraction activates them. Soften to the thermoregulatory point ('it no longer keeps us warm') and the fact stands. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

text: Goosebumps and standing hair are the same reflex a cat uses to look bigger. On us it achieves nothing at all, which is quite funny.

review.notes: Established paediatrics - greater bone plasticity and the greenstick pattern. Safe framing, no comparison of bodies, and it explains a difference a nine-year-old may have direct experience of. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

text: Children's bones bend further before they break than adults' do, which is why a child's fracture is often a crack rather than a clean snap.

review.notes: The anticipatory cardiorespiratory response is real and well documented, so the substance is sound, but the two sentences contradict each other as written: the first denies that the decision to run raises heart rate, and the second says the rise comes 'from the intention alone'. At min_age 9 that is not a rhetorical flourish, it is a comprehension failure. The opening negation also reads as denying that the work itself drives heart rate during running, which is the main effect. DEPTH CORRECTED sourced->read: the review record checked no sources.

text: Your heart does not beat faster because you decided to run. It starts climbing before the first step, from the intention alone.
